📄 Complete Details & Notification

The Kerala Public Service Commission (KPSC) has published the shortlist of candidates provisionally eligible for interview for the post of Higher Secondary School Teacher (Junior) Sanskrit - Statewide under Category No. 709/2025. The notification (SL.No. 156/2026/ERIX) was issued on 21/07/2026 from the KPSC Head Office, Thiruvananthapuram. This article gives you the complete, official register number list, cut-off mark, category-wise breakup, and the next steps you need to follow.

Kerala PSC Teacher Result 2026 - Download link

The Kerala PSC Teacher Result 2026 has been released for the Higher Secondary School Teacher (Junior) Sanskrit (Category No. 709/2025) recruitment. Candidates who appeared for the online examination held on 12 May 2026 can now download the official shortlist PDF and check their register numbers for the interview round.

Download Kerala PSC Teacher Result 2026

Main List - Register Numbers

  • 106031, 106083, 106115, 106119, 106136, 106154
  • 106193, 106201, 106260, 106268, 106272, 106275
  • 106281, 106297, 106300, 106319, 106322, 106325
  • 106334, 106344, 106346, 106369, 106372, 106377
  • 106391, 106404, 106410, 106426, 106442, 106445

Required Documents for OTR Verification

Shortlisted candidates must be personally present with original documents for One Time Registration (OTR) Verification and interview. Depending on the category claimed, the following documents are required:

  • OBC candidates: Non-Creamy Layer Certificate as per G.O.(P) No.81/09/SCSTDD dated 26.09.2009, or the certificate obtained through the e-district portal in the format prescribed in GO(Rt) No.3942/2018/RD dated 24.09.2018.
  • SC/ST candidates: Community Certificate in Form III, or a digitally signed certificate issued by a Revenue Authority not below the rank of a Tahsildar.
  • EWS candidates: EWS Certificate as per G.O.(MS) No.2/2020/P&ARD dated 12.02.2020, issued by the Revenue Authority.
  • All other original documents supporting the details furnished in the application, as required at the time of OTR verification.

How to Apply Next Steps for Shortlisted Candidates

This is a shortlist notification, not a fresh application notification, so there is no new "apply online" step at this stage. Shortlisted candidates should:

  1. Check their register number in the Main List, Supplementary List, or PwD list above.
  2. Keep all original certificates and documents ready as listed in the "Required Documents" section.
  3. Wait for the official schedule announcing the date, time, and venue of OTR Verification and interview, to be published separately by Kerala PSC.
  4. Visit the official Kerala PSC website regularly for updates.

Important Instructions

  • Inclusion of a register number in the Short List is purely provisional and subject to verification and scrutiny of the application on an absolute basis.
  • The Short List has been prepared by including candidates who secured the top marks in the Online Examination, based on details furnished by candidates in their application. Subsequent claims will not be entertained at any stage of selection.
  • Candidates who do not produce the required documents within the prescribed time limit, or whose applications are found defective, will be deleted from the Short List without further notice.
  • For this Online Examination, rechecking and revaluation are not allowed. However, a printout of the answer sheet will be issued to candidates who apply for it, on payment of the prescribed fee, after publication of the Ranked List. Detailed instructions on this will be furnished along with the Ranked List.

Haryana Staff Selection Commission (HSSC) has released a public notice announcing the list of candidates who have qualified the Physical Measurement Test (PMT) for various posts under Advertisement Nos. 13/2024, 01/2026, and 06/2026. The Physical Screening Test (PST) for these shortlisted candidates is scheduled to begin from 24 July 2026. This article explains the important dates, PST schedule, qualified/not-qualified categories, and how candidates can check their status and download their admit cards.

Add FJA on  As Preferred Source

HSSC PST 2026 Quick Overview

Particulars Details
Organization Haryana Staff Selection Commission (HSSC)

Test Name Physical Screening Test (PST)
PST Start Date 24 July 2026

Departments Covered Forest, Prison, Police
Official Website www.hssc.gov.in

About the HSSC PMT Result and PST Notice

This notice informs candidates who applied for posts such as Deputy Ranger, Warder (Male/Female), Assistant Superintendent Jail (Male/Female), Constable (General Duty), and Sub-Inspector (General Duty) about their PMT outcome. The list of candidates who qualified the PMT for Advt. Nos. 13/2024 and 06/2026 has been published in this notice. For Advt. 01/2026, the first part of the qualified list was published earlier via a public notice dated 11 June 2026, and the remaining qualified candidates have now been announced in this latest notice.

Candidates who appeared for the PMT but did not qualify are listed separately in Annexure-B of the official notice.

HSSC PST Schedule 2026 - PMT Qualified List Released

The Haryana Staff Selection Commission (HSSC) has released the PMT Qualified List and Physical Screening Test (PST) Schedule 2026 for various posts under Advertisement Nos. 13/2024, 01/2026, and 06/2026. Candidates who have qualified the Physical Measurement Test (PMT) can now check their registration number in the official PDF and appear for the Physical Screening Test (PST) starting from 24 July 2026. The official notice also includes the category-wise list of qualified candidates, PST schedule, reporting time, and important instructions. Candidates should download their PST admit card from the respective advertisement portal and carefully follow the schedule mentioned in the official notification.

How to Check the HSSC PMT Qualified List

The registration numbers of all qualified candidates, category-wise, are published in ascending order in the official notice. Since the list contains a large number of registration numbers across every post and department, candidates are advised to check their own registration number directly in the official PDF rather than relying on a summarised version.

  1. Visit the official HSSC website at www.hssc.gov.in.
  2. Look for the notice titled "Public Notice for PST for various posts against Advt. Nos. 13/2024, 01/2026 and 06/2026".
  3. Open the PDF and use the search/find function (Ctrl+F) to locate your registration number under the relevant post and department.
  4. Check Annexure-B if you want to confirm the list of candidates who appeared but did not qualify the PMT.

The Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Services Selection Commission (UPSSSC) has released the UPSSSC Stenographer Result 2026 for the Mains Examination conducted under Advertisement No. 13-Exam/2024. Candidates who appeared for the written examination can now check their qualifying status by downloading the result PDF from the official website upsssc.gov.in. The result contains the roll numbers of candidates shortlisted for the next stage, which includes the Hindi Stenography and Typing Skill Test. Candidates are advised to download the result PDF, verify their roll number, and keep all required documents ready for the upcoming document verification process.

Direct Link to Download UPSSSC Stenographer Result 2026

How to Check UPSSSC Stenographer Result 2026

  1. Visit the official UPSSSC website: upsssc.gov.in.
  2. Go to the "Results" section on the homepage.
  3. Click on the link for UPSSSC Stenographer Mains Result 2026 (Advt No. 13-Exam/2024).
  4. The result opens as a PDF containing roll numbers of qualified candidates.
  5. Use Ctrl+F (or Cmd+F on Mac) to search your roll number in the PDF.
  6. Download and save the result PDF for future reference.

What to Do After the UPSSSC Stenographer Result 2026

  • Download and safely store your result PDF and printout.
  • Check whether you have been shortlisted for the Hindi Stenography and Typing Skill Test.
  • Start practicing Hindi shorthand and typing speed if you haven't already, since this stage is qualifying in nature.
  • Keep your UPSSSC PET 2023 score card, educational certificates, and CCC certificate ready for document verification.
  • Regularly check upsssc.gov.in for the skill test admit card and schedule.

  • Class 10th and 12th mark sheets and certificates
  • CCC / equivalent computer certificate
  • Category certificate (SC/ST/OBC/EWS), if applicable
  • PwBD certificate, if applicable
  • Domicile / residence certificate of Uttar Pradesh
  • Valid photo ID proof (Aadhaar Card, Voter ID, etc.)

  • No logistical flexibility: No request for change of exam date, shift, centre, or venue will be entertained under any circumstance. Plan your travel and stay in advance once your centre is confirmed.

The Institute of Banking Personnel Selection (IBPS) released the IBPS RRB Clerk Reserve List 2026 on 30th June 2026 for candidates who appeared in the CRP RRBs-XIV recruitment cycle. Candidates who were not allotted a bank in the main result can now log in to the official IBPS portal with their registration number and password/date of birth to check their provisional allotment status under the reserve list. The list currently covers 26 participating Regional Rural Banks (RRBs), and shortlisted candidates will also be informed through email and SMS on their registered contact details.

Add FJA on  As Preferred Source

What Is the IBPS RRB Clerk Reserve List 2026?

This section explains the purpose of the reserve list and why IBPS issues it after the main selection round.

A reserve list is a backup panel that IBPS prepares after declaring the final result of the CRP RRBs-XIV exam. Once the primary list of selected candidates is allotted to participating banks, some vacancies remain unfilled because certain selected candidates do not join within the deadline, resign shortly after joining, or get rejected at the document verification stage. To ensure every sanctioned post is filled, IBPS draws candidates from the reserve panel, based on merit, category, and the number of vacancies still open, and provisionally allots them to a Regional Rural Bank for the Office Assistant/Customer Service Associate (Clerk) post.

Candidates who appeared in the IBPS RRB Clerk Mains exam but did not feature in the original selection list can check their status through the official IBPS portal. Login requires your Registration Number/Roll Number and Password/Date of Birth.

IBPS RRB Clerk Reserve List 2026 Login Link (Active)

How to Check IBPS RRB Clerk Reserve List 2026 Online?

This section outlines the step-by-step process to view and download your reserve list allotment status.

  1. Visit the official IBPS website at ibps.in.
  2. Click on the "CRP-CSA (Customer Service Associate)" tab on the homepage.
  3. Select "CRP-CRP XIV – Provisional Allotment under Reserve List."
  4. Enter your Registration Number/Roll Number and Password/Date of Birth.
  5. Fill in the captcha code and click on the Login button.
  6. View your allotment status and download the result for future reference.

How Will You Know If You're Selected?

This section explains how IBPS notifies candidates who get provisional allotment through the reserve list.

Candidates who are provisionally allotted a bank through the reserve list will receive an official communication via email and SMS on their registered email ID and mobile number. It is advisable to regularly check your registered contact details and the official IBPS portal so you don't miss any update.

What Happens After the Reserve List Allotment?

This section explains the next stages candidates must complete after receiving a provisional allotment.

Getting your name on the reserve list does not mean final selection it is a provisional allotment that becomes confirmed only after the bank completes verification. The typical process that follows includes:

  • Document Verification: Submission of original certificates and identity proofs for cross-checking.
  • Submission of Required Certificates: Educational, category, and other eligibility-related documents as specified by the allotted bank.
  • Medical Examination: Some banks may require a fitness check before final confirmation.
  • Joining Formalities: Completion of paperwork and reporting to the allotted branch.
  • Induction/Training Process: Orientation and training conducted by the bank before you begin regular duties.

Candidates should keep all original and photocopied documents ready in advance to avoid last-minute issues during verification.

Why Does IBPS Release a Reserve List?

This section explains the broader purpose behind the reserve list mechanism in IBPS recruitment.

A reserve list helps maintain smooth recruitment by ensuring sanctioned vacancies don't remain vacant. It benefits candidates who narrowly missed the initial cut-off by giving them another opportunity, while also helping banks manage manpower requirements efficiently across states and categories.

The Central Bank of India has announced a total of 4,500 Apprentice vacancies for the financial year 2026-27, distributed across various states and union territories. Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh reportedly have the largest state-wise allocations. Candidates are advised to refer to the official notification PDF on the bank's recruitment page for the exact state-wise and category-wise vacancy breakup, since detailed figures for every state were not confirmed in the sources reviewed for this article.

Eligibility Criteria

Candidates must meet the educational qualification, age limit, and nationality conditions set by the Central Bank of India to be eligible for the Apprentice post.

Educational Qualification

  • A graduation degree (bachelor's degree) in any discipline from a recognised university or institute.
  • Candidates should have completed graduation on or after 1 January 2022 (some sources indicate the cut-off as 1 January 2021; candidates should verify the exact date on the official notification).
  • Candidates with one year or more of work or training experience after graduation are not eligible, since this scheme is meant for fresh graduates.
  • Candidates who have already completed apprenticeship training, or are currently undergoing apprenticeship training elsewhere, are not eligible.
  • Basic computer knowledge is required.
  • Candidates must be proficient in the local language of the state they are applying for.

Age Limit

Candidates must be between 20 and 28 years of age as on 31 May 2026, meaning they should be born between 31 May 1998 and 31 May 2006 (both dates inclusive).

Category Age Relaxation

Candidates should check the official notification for the exact category-wise age relaxation applicable to them.

Salary / Stipend Details

Selected apprentices will receive a fixed monthly stipend of ₹15,000 during the 12-month training period. This is a training stipend rather than a regular salary, and no other allowances or benefits are provided. Completion of the apprenticeship does not guarantee permanent employment with the bank.

Application Fee

The exact application fee amount for the CBI Apprentice Recruitment 2026 was not confirmed in the sources reviewed for this article. Candidates should refer to the official Central Bank of India Apprentice notification PDF on centralbank.bank.in for accurate, category-wise fee details, since this cannot be reliably stated here.

Selection Process

The Central Bank of India Apprentice selection process involves two stages:

  1. Online Written Examination: An objective-type computer-based test with no negative marking for wrong answers.
  2. Local Language Proficiency Test: Candidates who qualify the online exam may need to appear for a test assessing reading, writing, and speaking skills in the local language of the applied state. Candidates who studied the local language at Class 10 or Class 12 level may be exempted from this test, subject to document verification.

Final selection also depends on document verification and meeting the required medical fitness standards set by the bank.

Documents Required at the Exam Centre

  • Printed copy of the CBI Apprentice Admit Card 2026
  • A valid original government-issued photo ID proof, such as Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Passport, Voter ID, or Driving Licence
  • A photocopy of the photo ID for verification
  • Recent passport-size photographs, as specified in the admit card instructions

Candidates should ensure the name on their ID proof matches the name printed on the admit card to avoid denial of entry.

How to Download the CBI Apprentice Admit Card 2026

Follow these steps to download your Central Bank of India Apprentice hall ticket:

  1. Visit the official website of the Central Bank of India at centralbankofindia.co.in or centralbank.bank.in.
  2. Go to the "Recruitment" or "Careers" section on the homepage.
  3. Click on the "CBI Apprentice Admit Card 2026" or "Download Call Letter" link.
  4. Enter your Registration Number/Roll Number and Password or Date of Birth.
  5. Fill in the captcha code, if required.
  6. Click the Login or Submit button.
  7. Your CBI Apprentice Hall Ticket 2026 will appear on the screen.
  8. Carefully verify all details, including your name, photograph, signature, exam date, and exam centre.
  9. Download the admit card and take a clear printout on an A4 sheet for the examination.

The online written examination consists of 100 objective-type questions worth 100 marks, to be completed in 60 minutes, with no negative marking.

  • Carry the printed admit card; digital copies on a phone or tablet are typically not accepted.

NMDC Steel Limited Recruitment 2026: Selection Process

Candidates will be required to appear for a Computer Based Test (CBT) consisting of Multiple-Choice Questions at centres decided by the Management. Based on the CBT score and requirement, candidates will be shortlisted discipline-wise, category-wise for Group Discussion (GD) & Interview.

Component Weightage
CBT (Computer Based Test) in concerned discipline 70%
Group Discussion (GD) 15%
Interview 15%

The CBT will be conducted in Hindi & English and will consist of objective-type multiple-choice questions. Minimum qualifying marks in CBT to be considered for GD & Interview: 40 marks for SC/ST/PwBD, 45 marks for OBC-NCL, and 50 marks for UR/EWS category.

Candidates will be called for GD & Interview based on CBT marks, discipline-wise and category-wise, in the ratio of 1:3. Where two or more candidates in the same discipline and category secure equal marks in CBT and the 1:3 ratio is exceeded, all candidates with equal marks will be called for GD & Interview irrespective of the ratio. Topics for Group Discussion will be decided in advance by the GD Committee and may be discipline-specific or general; GDs will be held discipline-wise and category-wise in batches.

Before joining, candidates must undergo a Pre-Employment Medical Examination by NSL's recognized hospital(s); the decision of NSL Management will be final and binding, and no relaxation in health standards is allowed.

Selected candidates will be posted at NMDC Steel Ltd, Nagarnar, Chhattisgarh, and may be assigned job/function/assignments as per the business requirement of the Company, at any stage during their service.

  • Caste/Category Certificate — SC/ST/OBC(NCL)/EWS/Disability/Ex-Serviceman Certificate, as applicable

Category (SC/ST/OBC-NCL/EWS/PwBD) once filled in the application form will not be changed, and no benefit of another category will be admissible later.

How to Apply for NMDC Steel Limited Recruitment 2026

  2. The application link will be available from 10:00 AM on 22.07.2026 to 11:45 PM on 11.08.2026.
  3. Fill all details online and upload the relevant documents/certificates as listed above.

AAI Recruitment 2026 Notification Out

AAI Recruitment 2026 Application Fee

  • Application Fee: Rs. 1,000 (inclusive of GST), payable through online mode only.
  • SC candidates, ST candidates, PwBD candidates, Women candidates, and AAI Apprentices who have completed 1 year of Apprenticeship Training in AAI are exempt from the fee.
  • Fee can be paid via Debit Card, Credit Card, Internet Banking, IMPS, or Cash Cards/Mobile Wallets.
  • Fees once paid are non-refundable under any circumstances; duplicate payments will be refunded after the closing date.
  • Candidates can apply for multiple posts with separate registration and separate fee payment for each post.

AAI Recruitment 2026 Selection Process

  • Computer Based Test (Objective Type) will be conducted for all posts, with no negative marking for wrong answers.
  • Provisionally eligible candidates will be called for the Computer Based Test based on details furnished in the application form.
  • The Computer Based Test will be followed by Application Verification/Subsequent Tests for all posts.
  • Post Codes 1 to 11 (all Manager posts) will also include an Interview as part of the selection process.
  • For Manager (Fire Services), Application Verification is followed by a Physical Measurement Test, Driving Test, and Physical Endurance Test (Running, Casualty Carrying, Pole Climbing, Rope Climbing, and Ladder Climbing & Descending). Only candidates who qualify these tests proceed to the interview.
  • For Manager and Junior Executive (Airport Operations), a valid Light Motor Vehicle License is essential (temporary/learning license not accepted).
  • Final selection is based on a merit list from Computer Based Test and Interview scores (wherever applicable), subject to meeting all eligibility criteria.
  • Selected candidates for Manager (Fire Services) must undergo training and execute a Surety Bond of Rs. 5 lakh to serve AAI for 3 years after training completion.
  • Colour blindness and/or night blindness is a rejection criterion for all posts except Post Codes 3 (Finance) and 12 (Junior Executive Finance).
  • Selected candidates will be liable to be posted anywhere in India.

Documents Required for AAI Recruitment 2026

  • Scanned photograph, signature, left thumb impression, and hand-written declaration (as per prescribed specifications)
  • Educational qualification certificates and mark sheets
  • Caste Certificate [SC/ST/OBC(NCL)], valid for FY 2026-27, where applicable
  • EWS Certificate, valid for FY 2026-27, where applicable
  • Disability Certificate (generated through Swavalamban/UDID portal) for PwBD candidates
  • Discharge Certificate for Ex-servicemen candidates
  • Experience Certificate and supporting documents proving the nature and duration of work experience
  • Apprentice Certificate from AAI, where applicable
  • No Objection Certificate (NOC) from current employer, for candidates already working in Central/State Government, Autonomous Body, or PSU

How to Apply for AAI Recruitment 2026?

  1. Visit the official website: www.aai.aero and go to the "CAREERS" tab.
  2. Keep ready a valid personal email ID, mobile number, scanned photograph, signature, left thumb impression, and hand-written declaration as per specifications.
  3. Fill in the online application form with accurate personal, educational, and experience details.
  4. Upload all required documents as per the eligibility criteria for the post.
  5. Pay the application fee of Rs. 1,000 online (if applicable), using the integrated payment gateway.
  6. Verify all details carefully before final submission, as no changes are possible after submitting.
  7. Take a printout of the e-Receipt and the online application form containing fee details, for your own record (no need to send it to AAI).
  8. Regularly check your registered email (including spam folder) and the AAI website for admit card and further updates.

AAI Recruitment 2026 Important Instructions

  • Only Indian Nationals fulfilling the eligibility criteria can apply.
  • Age, qualification, experience, and all other eligibility criteria will be reckoned as on 07 September 2026 (cut-off date).
  • Candidates should apply only if the final result of their required qualification has already been declared; there is no relaxation on this account.
  • OBC (NCL), EWS, SC/ST, and Disability certificates must be valid and in the prescribed Government of India format, produced at the time of Application Verification/Interview.
  • Candidates can apply for multiple posts, with separate registration and fee payment for each post.
  • Furnishing wrong or false information will lead to disqualification, and AAI will not be responsible for any consequence of such information.
  • No TA/DA will be paid for appearing in the Computer Based Test.
  • The Computer Based Test will be bilingual (Hindi and English), except for the language test itself.
  • AAI reserves the right to modify, alter, restrict, enlarge, or cancel the recruitment process at any time without prior notice.
  • Court of jurisdiction for any dispute will be at Delhi.

Eligibility for IBPS Specialist Officer Recruitment 2026 depends on the specific post applied for, since each role has a distinct educational qualification requirement. Age limits, however, remain uniform across all six posts, with relaxations available for reserved categories.

IBPS Specialist Officer Selection Process 2026

Selection under IBPS CRP SPL-XVI 2026 follows a three-stage process: Online Preliminary Examination, Online Main Examination, and a Common Interview. Only candidates who clear each stage progress to the next, and the final merit list is based on Main Examination and Interview scores combined.

  1. Online Preliminary Examination – Tentatively in August 2026; candidates must clear individual cut-offs in each of four tests.
  2. Preliminary Result – Declared in September/October 2026.
  3. Online Main Examination – Tentatively in November 2026; scores from this stage alone are used for interview shortlisting and final merit.
  4. Main Exam Result – Declared in November 2026.
  5. Common Interview – Conducted by Participating Banks and coordinated by Nodal Banks in November/December 2026; total 100 marks with minimum qualifying marks of 40% (35% for SC/ST/OBC/PwBD).
  6. Provisional Allotment – Expected in January 2027, based on merit-cum-preference with an 80:20 weightage between Main Exam and Interview.

Exam Pattern Overview

The Preliminary Exam for IT Officer, Agricultural Field Officer, HR/Personnel Officer, and Marketing Officer consists of 100 questions for 125 marks across English Language, Reasoning, Quantitative Aptitude, and Professional Knowledge, to be completed in 80 minutes. The Main Exam for the same posts carries 150 objective questions for 200 marks plus a Descriptive Paper of 25 marks, totaling 225 marks in 155 minutes. Candidates can apply for IBPS Specialist Officer Recruitment 2026 only through the online mode on the official IBPS website; no other application method is accepted. The steps below outline the complete registration and payment process.

  1. Visit the official website www.ibps.in and click on the "CRP SPL" link on the homepage.
  2. Select "Click Here to Apply Online for CRP-Specialist Officers (CRP SPL-XVI)" to open the application form.
  3. Click "Click Here for New Registration" and enter basic details to generate a Provisional Registration Number and Password.
  4. Log in again using the provisional credentials to complete the application form.
  5. Upload photograph, signature, left thumb impression, handwritten declaration, and SSC/SSLC/10th standard certificate as per specifications.
  6. Capture and upload a live photograph via webcam or mobile phone.
  7. Verify all details carefully, since no changes are allowed after clicking "Complete Registration" (except during the 2-day Edit Window).
  8. Pay the applicable application fee online via Debit Card, Credit Card, Net Banking, or UPI.
  9. Download and print the system-generated application form and e-receipt for future reference.

IBPS Specialist Officer Salary and Pay Scale 2026

IBPS CRP SPL-XVI Document Requirements

Shortlisted candidates must produce original documents along with self-attested photocopies at the time of interview, failing which their candidature can be cancelled. OBC candidates must submit a Non-Creamy Layer certificate issued on or after 01.04.2026, while EWS candidates need an Income & Asset Certificate valid for the year 2026-27 for financial year 2025-26.

Common Mistakes to Avoid While Applying for IBPS CRP SPL-XVI

Many candidates lose their chance at IBPS Specialist Officer Recruitment 2026 due to avoidable errors during the application process. Being aware of these common mistakes in advance can help ensure a smooth, error-free submission.

  • Applying for multiple posts: A candidate can apply for only one post; multiple applications are summarily rejected.

The Indian Army has invited online applications from unmarried women holding an NCC 'C' Certificate, and Wards of Battle Casualties of Indian Army personnel, for Short Service Commission (Non-Technical) under the NCC Special Entry Scheme, 125th Course (April 2027) - SSCW (NCC)-125. Indian Army NCC Special Entry Scheme 125: Quick Overview

Particulars Details
Type of Entry NCC Special Entry Scheme – 125th Course (April 2027), Short Service Commission (NT), Women (including Wards of Battle Casualties)
Age 19 to 25 years as on 01 January 2027
Open For Unmarried female graduates
Educational Qualification Graduation degree and minimum 'B' Grade in NCC 'C' Certificate exam
Vacancies 06 (05 General + 01 Wards of Battle Casualties)
Selection Process Application → Shortlisting → SSB → Medical → Merit List → Joining Letter
Pre-Commission Training Academy Officers Training Academy, Chennai
Duration of Training 49 weeks from April 2027
Stipend During Training ₹56,100 per month
Rank After Training Lieutenant
Salary on Commissioning CTC approx. ₹17–18 lakh per annum

Important Dates

  • Online application opens: 21 July 2026, 1500 hrs
  • Online application closes: 21 August 2026, 1500 hrs
  • SSB shortlisting (tentative): First week of September 2026
  • SSB Centre and date selection window: 14 days in September 2026 (first-come-first-served)
  • SSB interviews (tentative): November/December 2026, maximum 5 days
  • Course commencement: April 2027
  • Deadline to submit final degree certificate (final-year candidates): 01 April 2027

Vacancy Details

Category Vacancies
General Category (Women) 05
Wards of Battle Casualties of Indian Army Personnel 01
Total 06

The Indian Army notifies vacancies separately for each entry and gender based on operational and administrative requirements. The shortlisting process, cut-offs, and merit for men and women are independent of each other.

Also Read: Indian Army Agniveer UHQ Rally 2026

Eligibility Criteria

Nationality

The candidate must be: (i) a citizen of India, or (ii) a subject of Nepal, or (iii) a person of Indian origin who has migrated from Pakistan, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, or specified East African countries (Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Zambia, Malawi, Zaire, Ethiopia) and Vietnam, with the intention of permanently settling in India, provided a certificate of eligibility has been issued by the Government of India (not required for Gorkha subjects of Nepal).

Age Limit

19 to 25 years as on 01 January 2027 (born not earlier than 02 January 2002 and not later than 01 January 2008, both dates inclusive). The date of birth recorded in the Matriculation/Secondary School Examination Certificate at the time of application will be treated as final; no subsequent change request will be entertained.

Educational Qualification and NCC Criteria (For NCC 'C' Certificate Holders)

  • Minimum qualification: a Bachelor's degree or equivalent from a recognized university. Final-year candidates may apply, provided they complete their degree before the course begins; the aggregate percentage from the first two/three years of the degree course will be considered for shortlisting.
  • Minimum two/three years of service (as applicable) in the Senior Division/Wing of NCC.
  • Minimum 'B' Grade in the NCC 'C' Certificate exam. Candidates without an NCC 'C' Certificate (or only a Provisional NCC 'C' Certificate) on the date of application are not eligible. Provisional certificates are not accepted at the SSB stage.

Important: Candidates may appear for only one SSB interview - either as a CDSE candidate for SSCW (NT) (Women)-125 Course, or for NCC (Special) Entry-125 Course (Women). An undertaking to this effect must be given in the online application.

Eligibility for Wards of Battle Casualties

  • Available to unmarried sons and unmarried daughters (including legally adopted) of Army personnel classified as: killed in action; died of wounds/injuries (other than self-inflicted); wounded/injured (other than self-inflicted); or missing, presumed dead.
  • Educational qualification: Graduate degree from a recognized university (final-year candidates also eligible under the same conditions as above).
  • NCC 'C' Certificate is not required for this category.
  • Required documents: Battle Casualty certificate number issued by the Manpower (Policy & Planning) Directorate (or Adjutant General's Branch MP-5(D) for casualties after September 2013); copy of Part II Order classifying the casualty as a "Battle Casualty"; and a Relationship Certificate issued by the Manpower Directorate/Regimental Records.

Age Limit and Physical Standards

Age limit is detailed above. Candidates must also meet minimum physical standards before joining the training academy:

Activity Minimum Standard (Women)
2.4 km run 13 minutes
Push-ups 15
Pull-ups 02
Sit-ups 25
Squats Two sets of 30 repetitions
Lunges Two sets of 10 repetitions
Swimming Should know fundamentals of swimming

Salary and Pay Scale

Rank Pay Level Pay (₹)
Lieutenant Level 10 56,100 – 1,77,500
Captain Level 10B 61,300 – 1,93,900
Major Level 11 69,400 – 2,07,200
Lieutenant Colonel Level 12A 1,21,200 – 2,12,400
Colonel Level 13 1,30,600 – 2,15,900
Brigadier Level 13A 1,39,600 – 2,17,600
Major General Level 14 1,44,200 – 2,18,200
  • Stipend during training: ₹56,100 per month (fixed at OTA, Chennai for the full 49-week duration).
  • Military Service Pay (MSP): ₹15,500 per month, fixed, for officers from Lieutenant to Brigadier.
  • Approximate CTC on commissioning: ₹17–18 lakh per annum, excluding free medical cover and one home-town visit per year.
  • Additional allowances include Dearness Allowance, Transport Allowance, Children Education Allowance (₹2,250/month per child, for two eldest children), Hostel Subsidy (₹6,750/month per child), Dress Allowance (₹20,000/year), and various field/hardship allowances depending on posting.

Promotion Criteria

Rank Promotion Criteria
Lieutenant On commission
Captain On completion of 2 years reckonable commissioned service
Major On completion of 6 years reckonable commissioned service
Lieutenant Colonel On completion of 13 years reckonable commissioned service
Colonel (TS) On completion of 26 years reckonable commissioned service
Colonel and above On selection basis, subject to fulfilment of requisite service conditions

Tenure and Release Options

  • Officers are liable to serve for 10 years, extendable by a further 4 years, subject to eligibility and organizational requirements.
  • Permanent Commission may be considered in the 10th year of service.
  • Officers may apply for release during the 5th year of service; Army HQ's decision on such applications is final.
  • Release options are also available after the 10th and 14th years of service.
  • Reserve liability: Officers released before completion of contractual service must serve the Army Reserve for 5 years, plus 2 years on a voluntary basis, or up to age 37 (whichever is earlier).

Selection Process

  1. Shortlisting of applications: Based on bonus marks out of a maximum of 100 - up to 50 marks for NCC 'C' Certificate grading (50 for 'A' Grade, 25 for 'B' Grade) and up to 50 marks for graduation performance (0 to 50 marks on a sliding scale from below 60% to 85%+ aggregate).
  2. Vacancy-to-call-up ratio: Candidates are shortlisted for SSB based on this ratio, decided by the Directorate General of Recruiting.
  3. SSB Centre and date selection: Shortlisted candidates choose their SSB centre and date on a first-come-first-served basis; choices cannot be changed later except under exceptional circumstances.
  4. SSB interview: Conducted over 5 days at Prayagraj, Bhopal, Bengaluru, or Jalandhar. Candidates undergo a two-stage process - Stage I, and Stage II (for those who clear Stage I). Candidates who fail Stage I are sent back the same day.
  5. Medical examination: Conducted for candidates recommended after Stage II.
  6. Merit list: Prepared based on SSB marks. Ties are broken first by age (older candidate ranked higher), then by percentage in the qualifying exam.
  7. Joining letter: Issued to candidates within the merit list and available vacancies, subject to meeting all eligibility criteria and being declared medically fit.

Candidates who fail to report within 7 days of the reporting date will have their candidature cancelled, and the next candidate in the merit list will be considered.

Required Documents

  • Signed printout of the online application with self-attested photograph
  • Matriculation/Secondary School Examination Certificate (or equivalent) and mark sheet
  • 12th Class certificate and mark sheet
  • Graduation degree or provisional degree certificate (provisional degree must not be older than 6 months as on 01 April 2027, i.e., issued between 01 October 2026 and 01 April 2027)
  • Mark sheets of all years/semesters
  • NCC 'C' Certificate, issued on or before the date of online application submission (not required for Wards of Battle Casualties)
  • CGPA-to-percentage conversion certificate from the university, where applicable
  • For final-year candidates: certificate from the institution head confirming final-year status and expected result declaration by 01 April 2027
  • For Wards of Battle Casualties: Battle Casualty certificate, Part II Order copy, and Relationship Certificate

Note: DigiLocker certificates will not be accepted in place of original certificates. All originals must be carried to the SSB interview; incomplete documents lead to summary rejection.

How to Apply

  1. Visit www.joinindianarmy.nic.in and click "Officer Entry Application/Login," then "Registration" (skip if already registered).
  2. After registration, click "Apply Online" under the Dashboard, then click "Apply" against Short Service Commission NCC Special Entry Course.
  3. Fill in personal information, communication details, education details, and previous SSB details (if any), clicking "Save & Continue" after each section.
  4. Review the summary of your information, then click "Submit" only after confirming all details are correct.
  5. Take two printouts of the application (with roll number) 30 minutes after the online application closes on the last day.

No changes can be made to the application after it closes. Candidates must submit only one application - multiple applications will result in cancellation.

Also Read: Indian Army NCC Special Entry Scheme 125th Course (Men) Recruitment 2026 - Apply Online for 70 Posts

Important Instructions

  • Candidate's name, parents' names, and date of birth in the profile and application must exactly match the Matriculation/Secondary certificate; any variation leads to cancellation.
  • CGPA/grades must be converted to marks per the university's formula; discrepancies found later lead to cancellation.
  • Candidates cannot marry during training, nor live with parents/guardians during the training period; marrying before or during training leads to removal and recovery of training costs.
  • Cost of training at OTA is borne by the Government, except for candidates withdrawn for personal reasons or reasons within their control, who must refund training costs at ₹20,482 per week (as of 2026).
  • Candidates serving in the Armed Forces must inform their Commanding Officer in writing about applying, and carry a countersigned application to the SSB.
  • Candidates should never have been debarred by UPSC from any exam, arrested/convicted by a criminal court, or expelled from any service training academy on disciplinary grounds.
  • Travelling Allowance (AC 3-Tier fare) is admissible only for the first SSB appearance for a particular type of commission.
  • Successful completion of training at OTA, Chennai earns a Post Graduate Diploma in Defence Management and Strategic Studies from the University of Madras.

ISRO Recruitment 2026 Eligibility Criteria

Educational Qualification – Assistant / Upper Division Clerk (Post No. 1, 3, 5)

  • Graduation must have been completed within the minimum stipulated duration of the course as prescribed by the University
  • Proficiency in the use of computers

Educational Qualification – Junior Personal Assistant / Stenographer (Post No. 2, 4, 6)

  • Graduation with a minimum of 60% marks or CGPA of 6.32 on a 10-point scale, completed within the minimum stipulated duration of the course, OR
  • Diploma in Commercial/Secretarial Practice with a minimum of 60% marks or CGPA of 6.32 on a 10-point scale, completed within the minimum stipulated duration, plus one year of experience as Steno-Typist/Stenographer
  • A minimum speed of 60 w.p.m. in English Shorthand/Stenography
  • Proficiency in the use of computers

Candidates holding a Diploma in Commercial Practice (DCP) or Diploma in Commercial and Computer Practice (DCCP), along with an Apprenticeship Training Certificate issued by the Board of Apprenticeship Training (BOAT) under the National Apprenticeship Training Scheme (Apprenticeship Act 1961), will have this considered equivalent to one year of Steno-Typist/Stenographer experience.

CGPA/Percentage Reckoning Rules

  • Where a University's Degree Certificate or Consolidated Mark-sheet mentions both CGPA and percentage, at least one of the two criteria must meet ISRO/DOS eligibility norms.
  • Where only CGPA is mentioned, the CGPA itself must meet ISRO/DOS eligibility criteria; conversion of CGPA to percentage is not permitted for determining eligibility, regardless of any conversion formula prescribed by the University.
  • For Dual/Integrated Degree Programmes, if CGPA/percentage for Graduation and Post-Graduation are mentioned separately, the Graduation-level figure is reckoned.
  • If a common CGPA/percentage is given for the entire Dual/Integrated Degree course, that combined figure is used for eligibility.
  • Where no CGPA/percentage formula is prescribed for a Dual/Integrated Degree, the cumulative CGPA/percentage as per the Final/Consolidated Mark Sheet applies.
  • These rules apply uniformly irrespective of whether the University prescribes a conversion formula.

Union Bank of India Recruitment 2026: Selection Process

For posts up to Scale III, selection may comprise Online Examination, Group Discussion (if required), and/or Personal Interview, depending on the number of applicants. For posts in Scale IV, V, and VI, selection may comprise Group Discussion (if required), any other test/assessment, and/or Personal Interview. The Bank reserves the right to add, cancel, or modify the selection method for any notified post.

Online Examination Structure - Specialist Officers (Post Codes S01–S108, up to Scale III)

Test No. of Questions Maximum Marks Duration
Professional Knowledge relevant to the post 50 (MCQ) 100 60 minutes

Online Examination Structure - General Banking Officers (Post Codes G01–G19, up to Scale III)

Test No. of Questions Maximum Marks Duration
Quantitative Aptitude 25 25 120 minutes
Reasoning 25 25
English Language 25 25
Professional Knowledge relevant to the post/domain 50 100
Total 125 175  

Quantitative Aptitude, Reasoning, and English Language sections are qualifying in nature - marks in these are not counted toward final merit. All tests except English Language are available bilingually (English and Hindi). Minimum qualifying marks: 40% for General/EWS categories, 35% for reserved categories (SC/ST/OBC/PwBD), subject to the Bank's discretion. There is a penalty of 25% of the marks assigned to a question for each wrong answer; unattempted questions carry no penalty.

Personal Interview

A Personal Interview of 100 marks assesses academic and job knowledge, power of expression, clarity of thought, leadership qualities, communication skills, and suitability for the post. Minimum qualifying marks: 50 for General/EWS, 45 for Reserved Category (SC/ST/OBC/PwBD). Candidates are called for interview in the ratio of 1:3 against the number of vacancies (subject to change at the Bank's discretion).

Final Merit

Final selection is based on the aggregate marks of Online Examination and Personal Interview (or Personal Interview alone, or GD/other assessment plus Personal Interview, depending on which stages are conducted), prepared in descending order category-wise, up to the number of vacancies. In case of a tie, the candidate senior in age (earlier date of birth) is ranked higher.

  • Printout of the valid Interview Call Letter
  • System-generated printout of the online application form
  • Proof of Date of Birth (Birth Certificate or SSLC/Std. X Certificate with DOB)
  • Photo Identity Proof (PAN Card/Passport/Permanent Driving Licence/Voter's Card/Bank Passbook with photo/Aadhaar, etc. - Ration Card and Learner's Driving Licence are NOT accepted)
  • Mark sheets and certificates/degree for educational qualifications
  • Latest Caste Certificate (for SC/ST/OBC candidates, in prescribed Government format)
  • OBC Non-Creamy Layer certificate issued on or after 01.04.2026 (for OBC candidates)
  • Income & Asset Certificate based on FY 2025-26, valid for FY 2026-27 (for EWS candidates)
  • Disability certificate in prescribed format (for PwBD candidates)
  • Scribe declaration form, if services of a scribe were used
  • Discharge book/pension payment order (for Ex-servicemen)
  • No Objection Certificate from employer (for candidates serving in Government/PSU/Bank)
  • Experience certificate in the prescribed format (Annexure-II of the notification), issued by the Competent Authority of the employer, clearly stating period, post held, and nature of duties

Appointment letters, salary certificates, and pay slips are not accepted as proof of work experience.

Union Bank of India Recruitment 2026: How to Apply

  1. Visit the official website www.unionbankofindia.co.in and click on the 'Recruitment' page.
  2. On the Career Overview page, click 'Click to View the Current Recruitment' to open the link "UNION BANK RECRUITMENT PROJECT 2026-27 (OFFICERS WITH DOMAIN EXPERTISE, GENERAL BANKING OFFICERS & SPECIALIST OFFICERS)".
  3. Click on "CLICK HERE TO APPLY ONLINE" to open the online application form.
  4. Choose "Click here for New Registration" and enter your Name, contact details, and Email ID. Note down the system-generated Provisional Registration Number and Password.
  5. Use the "SAVE AND NEXT" option to fill the application in stages if needed, and verify all details carefully - no changes are allowed after clicking "COMPLETE REGISTRATION".
  6. Upload photograph, signature, and left thumb impression as per the prescribed specifications.
  7. Fill in the remaining application details, preview the form, and click "COMPLETE REGISTRATION".
  8. Click on the "Payment" tab and pay the applicable application fee online.
  9. Click 'Submit' and save/print the system-generated application form and e-receipt for future reference.

Candidates can apply for only one post. Only the last valid, complete application will be retained in case of multiple submissions. An application, once submitted, cannot be withdrawn, and the fee is non-refundable.

Union Bank of India Recruitment 2026: Important Instructions

  • Application can be made for only one post; multiple appearances for a single post at interview will lead to cancellation of candidature.
  • No change of category will be permitted at any stage after registration of the online application.
  • Existing Union Bank of India employees may apply through proper channel (HR Department of Regional/Zonal Office) and, if selected, must resign and rejoin the Bank's service afresh.
  • Selected candidates will be on probation for 2 years of active service.
  • Selected candidates for posts G01–G19 must execute a Service Indemnity Bond to serve the Bank for a minimum of 3 years, or pay ₹2,00,000 plus applicable taxes if they leave before completing 3 years.
  • Selected candidates for posts S01–S108 must execute a Service Indemnity Bond to serve the Bank for a minimum of 3 years, or pay ₹2,50,000 plus applicable taxes if they leave before completing 3 years.
  • Selected candidates shall be posted at any Branch/Office of the Bank throughout India at the Bank's sole discretion.
  • The Bank reserves the right to change/modify the number of vacancies, examination structure, or cancel the recruitment process at any stage.
  • Any dispute arising out of the notification is subject to the sole jurisdiction of courts in Mumbai.

IOB Apprentice Recruitment 2026-27 Eligibility Criteria

Candidates applying for IOB Apprentice Recruitment 2026-27 must be Citizens of India. Merely applying, being shortlisted, or appearing for document verification and personal interaction does not guarantee an offer of engagement in the Bank.

Educational Qualification

Candidates must hold a Degree (Graduation) in any discipline from a University recognized by the Government of India, or an equivalent qualification recognized by the Central Government. The result must be declared on or before 31.07.2026. Candidates registered under the National Apprenticeship Training Scheme (NATS) must have had their graduation result declared between 01.03.2022 and 31.07.2026, both dates inclusive, and must produce mark sheets and provisional or degree certificates when required.

Age Limit

The minimum age is 20 years and the maximum age is 28 years as on the cut-off date of 01.07.2026 for General and EWS category candidates, meaning the date of birth should fall between 01.07.1998 and 01.07.2006, both dates inclusive. Candidates registered under NAPS should be less than 34 years as on the cut-off date, after applicable relaxation.

Candidates must score a minimum aggregate percentage as decided by the Bank, with a 5 percent relaxation available for SC/ST/OBC/PwBD candidates. There is no minimum qualifying mark for individual subjects.

Test of Local Language

Candidates applying for a particular state must be proficient in reading, writing, speaking, and understanding at least one local language of that state. This test is conducted during document verification after qualifying the written examination. Candidates who have studied the specified local language up to 10th or 12th standard are exempted from this test.

Wait-list

A state-category-wise waitlist will be maintained for one year from the date of the result or the next engagement exercise, whichever is earlier.

📄 Complete Details & Notification

The Indian Army has released the NCC Special Entry Scheme 125th Course (April 2027) Recruitment 2026 notification for Short Service Commission (Non-Tech) posts, offering 70 vacancies (63 General + 7 for Wards of Battle Casualties of Army Personnel). Unmarried male graduates aged 19 to 25 years as on 01 January 2027, holding a minimum 'B' Grade in the NCC 'C' Certificate, can apply online from 20 July 2026 to 20 August 2026. Selected cadets receive a monthly stipend of ₹56,100 during training at OTA Chennai.

Add FJA on  As Preferred Source

Indian Army NCC Special Entry Scheme 125 Course PDF Download Link

Candidates who want to verify every clause before applying should download and read the complete NCC Special Entry Scheme 125th Course notification PDF directly from the official Indian Army recruiting website. The PDF carries full details on medical standards, physical fitness benchmarks, document checklists, and terms of engagement that are only summarised in this article.

  • Indian Army NCC Special Entry Scheme 125 Course Download PDF 

Indian Army Officer Recruitment 2026: Quick Overview

Candidates searching for a quick snapshot of the NCC Special Entry Scheme 125th Course Recruitment 2026 can refer to the table below. It summarises the organisation, post, total vacancies, application window, and mode of application in one place.

Detail Information
Recruiting Organisation Indian Army (Directorate General of Recruiting)
Name of Course/Entry NCC Special Entry Scheme – 125th Course (April 2027)
Post Short Service Commission (NT) for Men, including Wards of Battle Casualties
Total Vacancies 70 (63 General + 7 Wards of Battle Casualties)
Application Start Date 20 July 2026, 1500 hrs
Application Last Date 20 August 2026, 1500 hrs
Mode of Application Online only, via www.joinindianarmy.nic.in
Pre-Commission Training Academy Officers Training Academy (OTA), Chennai

Indian Army Officer Recruitment 2026 Important Dates 2026

Anyone tracking the NCC 125 Course last date and other key milestones should note the schedule below. These dates are as specified in the official notification and cover the application window through the likely SSB period.

Event Date

Indian Army NCC Special Entry Scheme 125 Course Vacancy 2026

The NCC Special Entry Scheme 125 Course vacancy 2026 stands at a total of 70 posts under the Short Service Commission (Non-Tech) category. These vacancies are split between general NCC candidates and a reserved category for wards of Army battle casualties.

Post Category Vacancies
SSC (NCC) - Men General (NCC 'C' Certificate holders) 63
SSC (NCC) - Men Wards of Battle Casualties of Indian Army Personnel 7
Total - 70

Candidates should also note that the Indian Army notifies vacancies separately for each entry and gender, and the final selection is purely based on the notified vacancies against the applications received for this specific course.

Indian Army NCC Special Entry Scheme 125 Course Eligibility 2026

Candidates wondering about eligibility for the NCC Special Entry Scheme 125th Course can note that the entry is open only to unmarried male graduates who meet specific age, nationality, and NCC certification requirements. Wards of Battle Casualties have a slightly relaxed set of conditions, explained separately below.

Nationality

A candidate must be a citizen of India, a subject of Nepal, or a person of Indian origin who has migrated from Pakistan, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, or specified East African countries with the intention of permanently settling in India, subject to a certificate of eligibility from the Government of India (not required for Gorkha subjects of Nepal).

Age Limit

Applicants must be between 19 and 25 years as on 01 January 2027, meaning candidates born not earlier than 02 January 2002 and not later than 01 January 2008 (both dates inclusive) are eligible. No age relaxation details beyond this are specified in the notification.

Educational Qualification and NCC Requirement

For NCC 'C' Certificate holders, the minimum qualification is a Bachelor's Degree from a recognised university, along with a minimum of 'B' Grade in the 'C' Certificate examination of NCC, after serving at least two/three years (as applicable) in the Senior Division/Wing of NCC. Final-year students may also apply, provided they complete their degree before the course begins; for such candidates, the aggregate percentage scored in the first two/three years of the degree course will be used for shortlisting. A provisional NCC 'C' Certificate will not be accepted at the SSB stage - candidates must hold the confirmed certificate before appearing for the interview.

Eligibility for Wards of Battle Casualties

Unmarried sons and unmarried daughters (including legally adopted) of Army personnel classified as Battle Casualties - killed in action, died of wounds, wounded/injured, or missing presumed dead - are eligible under a separate quota of 7 vacancies. The same graduation qualification applies, but an NCC 'C' Certificate is not required for this category.

Indian Army NCC Special Entry Scheme 125 Course Selection Process 2026

The selection procedure for the NCC Special Entry Scheme 125 Course follows a five-stage structure: Application, Shortlisting, SSB Interview, Medical Examination, and Merit List, followed by the Joining Letter. Each stage is explained below with the realistic timeline indicated in the notification.

  1. Shortlisting of Applications: Based on bonus marks out of a maximum of 100 - up to 50 marks for performance in the NCC 'C' Certificate (50 for 'A' Grade, 25 for 'B' Grade) and up to 50 marks for graduation performance (ranging from 0 for below 60% to 50 for 85% and above). Shortlisting is tentatively expected in the first week of September 2026.
  2. SSB Centre & Date Selection: Shortlisted candidates choose their SSB centre and date on a first-come-first-served basis during a 14-day window in September 2026.
  3. SSB Interview: Conducted over a maximum of five days at Prayagraj, Bhopal, Bengaluru, or Jalandhar, likely in November/December 2026. It follows a two-stage process - candidates who fail Stage I are returned the same day.
  4. Medical Examination: Candidates recommended after Stage II undergo a medical test; the medical validity period is 270 days from the SSB medical board date to the PCTA joining date.
  5. Merit List: Prepared strictly on SSB interview marks; ties are broken first by age (older candidate ranked higher) and then by qualifying exam percentage.
  6. Joining Letter: Issued to candidates within the merit list and available vacancies, subject to meeting all eligibility criteria, for Pre-Commission Training at OTA Chennai starting April 2027.

Indian Army NCC Special Entry Scheme 125 Course Apply Online 2026

Candidates looking to complete the NCC Special Entry Scheme 125 Course apply online process can follow the numbered steps below. Applications are accepted only through the official Indian Army recruiting website - no offline or hard-copy submissions are entertained.

  1. Visit www.joinindianarmy.nic.in and click on 'Officer Entry Application/Login'.
  2. Click 'Registration' and complete the registration form (skip this step if already registered on the portal).
  3. After registering, click 'Apply Online' under the Dashboard, then select 'Eligibility' on the Officers Selection page.
  4. Click 'Apply' against the "Short Service Commission NCC Special Entry Course" option.
  5. Fill in personal information, communication details, education details, and previous SSB details across each segment, clicking 'Save & Continue' after every section.
  6. Review all details on the 'Summary of your information' page and click 'Submit' only after confirming accuracy.
  7. Take two printouts of the submitted application (with Roll Number) 30 minutes after final closure of the online application on the last day.

Candidates must submit only one application; multiple applications from the same candidate will result in cancellation of candidature, with no representation entertained.

Salary and Pay Scale After Commissioning

Selected candidates commissioned as Lieutenant draw pay as per Level 10 (₹56,100 – ₹1,77,500) in the Defence Pay Matrix, along with Military Service Pay of ₹15,500 per month. The approximate CTC on commissioning is ₹17–18 lakh per annum, excluding free medical cover and one home-town travel benefit per year.

Rank Pay Level Pay Scale (₹)
Lieutenant Level 10 56,100 – 1,77,500
Captain Level 10B 61,300 – 1,93,900
Major Level 11 69,400 – 2,07,200
Lieutenant Colonel Level 12A 1,21,200 – 2,12,400
Colonel Level 13 1,30,600 – 2,15,900

During the 49-week training period at OTA Chennai, cadets receive a fixed stipend of ₹56,100 per month. On successful commissioning, this training period is not counted as commissioned service, though admissible allowance arrears for the training period are paid to cadets.

Documents Required at the Selection Centre

Candidates must carry originals along with self-attested copies of the following documents to the Selection Centre; DigiLocker certificates are not accepted in place of originals unless the issuing institution certifies that only e-certificates were issued.

  • Signed printout of the application with a self-attested photograph
  • Matriculation/Secondary School Examination Certificate and Mark Sheet
  • 12th Class Certificate and Mark Sheet
  • Graduation Degree/Provisional Degree from a recognised university (provisional degree not older than six months as on 01 April 2027)
  • Mark sheets of all years/semesters
  • NCC 'C' Certificate, issued on or before the date of online application submission (not required for Wards of Battle Casualties)
  • University certificate on CGPA-to-marks conversion criteria, where applicable
  • For final-year candidates, a certificate from the Principal/Head of Institution confirming the result will be declared by 01 April 2027
  • For Wards of Battle Casualties, additional documents including the Battle Casualty certificate and relationship certificate issued by the Manpower (Policy & Planning) Directorate

Common Mistakes to Avoid While Applying

Many applicants lose out on the NCC Special Entry Scheme 125 Course not due to ineligibility but due to avoidable errors during the application process. Keeping the following points in mind can help candidates avoid rejection.

  • Do not submit the application with a provisional NCC 'C' Certificate if it hasn't been upgraded to the final certificate before the SSB - it will not be accepted at that stage.
  • Double-check that your name, parents' names, and date of birth in the online application exactly match your Matriculation/Secondary School certificate, since any mismatch leads to cancellation.
  • Convert your CGPA to percentage using your university's official formula before filling in the "Marks obtained in Graduation" field, as discrepancies found later can cancel your candidature.
  • Once the application window closes, no corrections are entertained, so review the "Summary of your information" page carefully before hitting Submit.
  • Avoid submitting more than one application - the system treats multiple applications from the same candidate as grounds for cancellation, not deduplication.
  • Keep a buffer before the deadline; queries received less than three days before the closing date are not guaranteed a response.

Punjab National Bank (PNB) has invited online applications for recruitment to 545 posts of Local Bank Officer (LBO) in Junior Management Grade Scale-I (JMGS-I). The vacancies are distributed across 17 states, and candidates can apply for only one state based on their eligibility and language proficiency. This article covers all details of the notification, including state-wise vacancies, eligibility, salary, selection process, and how to apply.

PNB LBO Recruitment 2026: State-wise Vacancy Details

A total of 545 vacancies are notified across 17 states/UTs. Candidates must apply for only one state and must be proficient in the mandatory local language specified for that state. The Bank has clarified that the number of vacancies, including reserved category vacancies, is provisional and subject to change.

Key Points on Vacancy Distribution

  • Candidates belonging to reserved categories for which no vacancy has been announced in a state may apply against Unreserved (UR) vacancies of that state, if they meet UR eligibility criteria.
  • Candidates can apply for a vacancy in one state only. Applying against one state makes a candidate ineligible to apply against any other state.

  • Selected candidates will be posted within the selected state until completion of nine (9) years of service or promotion to SMG Scale IV, whichever is earlier.
  • Prior experience will not be considered for seniority in service.
  • PwBD reservation is on a horizontal basis; selected PwBD candidates will be placed in their applicable category (SC/ST/OBC/EWS/UR) and posted within the state applied for, at locations identified suitable by the Bank.

PNB LBO Recruitment 2026 Eligibility Criteria

Nationality/Citizenship

An applicant must be:

  • A citizen of India, or
  • A subject of Nepal, or
  • A subject of Bhutan, or
  • A Tibetan Refugee who came to India before 1st January 1962 with the intention of permanently settling in India, or
  • A person of Indian origin who has migrated from Pakistan, Burma, Sri Lanka, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Zambia, Malawi, Zaire, Ethiopia, or Vietnam with the intention of permanently settling in India.

Candidates in the last four categories must have a certificate of eligibility issued by the Government of India before the date of this notification, and must also be proficient in the local language of the state applied for.

Candidates who have completed their graduation in any discipline can also explore more Bank Officer Jobs and Graduate Government Jobs available across India.

Age and Educational Qualification

Post Scale Age (Years) Educational Qualification
Local Bank Officer (LBO) JMGS-I Min: 20, Max: 30 Graduate in any discipline from a University/Institution recognized/approved by the Government of India or its regulatory bodies

The candidate must possess a valid Mark-sheet/Degree Certificate confirming graduate status on the day of registration, and must indicate the percentage of marks obtained in Graduation while registering online.

Local Language Requirement

Candidates must be proficient in reading, writing, and speaking the specified local language of the state for which they are applying (as listed in the state-wise vacancy table). A Local Language Proficiency Test (LLPT) will be conducted by an external agency for candidates who have not studied the local language as a subject in Class 10 or Class 12.

Post-Qualification Experience

  • Candidates must possess a minimum of one year of post-qualification work experience in Clerical/Officer Cadre in any Scheduled Commercial Bank or Regional Rural Bank listed in the Second Schedule of the RBI Act, 1934.
  • One advance increment is payable for each completed prior year of service as an Officer in Scheduled Commercial Banks (subject to a maximum of 2 increments), if the job profile matches that of a Scale-I Generalist Officer of PNB.
  • Candidates from subsidiaries of Scheduled Commercial Banks (Officer cadre) are eligible for only one advance increment under the same condition.
  • Proof of prior experience must be submitted in the prescribed format, duly certified by the previous employer.
  • Experience in other financial institutions will not be considered if the job profile does not substantially match that of a PNB Scale-I Generalist Officer.
  • No prior service/experience will be considered for seniority purposes.

Cut-off Dates for Eligibility

  • Age: Reckoned as on 01.07.2026
  • Mandatory Experience: Reckoned as on the closing date for online registration, i.e., 09.08.2026
  • Educational Qualification: Reckoned as on the closing date for online registration, i.e., 09.08.2026
  • The result of the qualifying examination must have been declared on or before 09.08.2026.
  • Candidates must indicate the percentage obtained in Graduation to the nearest two decimals; CGPA/OGPA must be converted to percentage as per the university's official conversion formula. A fraction of percentage will be ignored (e.g., 59.99% will be treated as less than 60%).

The maximum age limit is applicable to Unreserved (UR) and EWS category candidates. Relaxation for SC/ST/OBC(NCL) is allowed cumulatively with only one of the remaining categories under (iii) to (v) above. Candidates seeking relaxation must submit the necessary certificates at the time of Interview and at any subsequent stage as required by the Bank.

PNB LBO Recruitment 2026: Salary and Perquisites

Selected candidates will draw pay in the scale of Rs. 48480-2000/7-62480-2340/2-67160-2680/7-85920 under JMGS-I. In addition to Basic Pay, selected candidates will be entitled to Dearness Allowance (DA), City Compensatory Allowance (CCA), HRA/Leased Accommodation, Leave Fare Concession, Medical Insurance, Retirement Benefits, and other perquisites as per Bank rules.

All others (UR/OBC(NCL)/EWS) Rs. 1000/- + GST @18% = Rs. 1180/-

Payment is accepted only through online mode (Debit Card, Credit Card, Internet Banking, IMPS, Cash Cards/Mobile Wallets, or UPI). Bank transaction charges for online payment are to be borne by the candidate. The fee, once paid, is non-refundable under any circumstances and cannot be reserved for any other examination.

PNB LBO Recruitment 2026 Selection Process

Selection for the post of Local Bank Officer shall be conducted in four phases. The Bank reserves the right to decide whether all or any of these modes shall be adopted:

  1. Online Written Test
  2. Screening
  3. Local Language Proficiency Test (LLPT), if applicable
  4. Personal Interview

Online Written Test Structure

Name of the Test No. of Questions Maximum Marks Sectional Duration (Minutes)
Reasoning & Computer Aptitude 25 25 35
Data Analysis & Interpretation 25 25 35
English Language 25 25 25
Quantitative Aptitude 25 25 35
General/Economy/Banking Awareness 50 50 50
  • There is negative marking: one-fourth of the marks assigned to each question is deducted for each wrong answer.
  • Minimum qualifying marks: 40% for General/EWS category, 35% for Reserved category, in each section. The Bank reserves the right to revise this at its discretion.

Screening

The online application and submitted documents of written-test-qualified candidates will be scrutinized to confirm eligibility before the Language Proficiency Test/Interview. Candidates found ineligible or with incorrect/false documents at any stage will be rejected from further participation.

Local Language Proficiency Test (LLPT)

  • Candidates who have not studied the applied-for state's local language as a subject in Class 10 or 12 must appear for the LLPT.
  • The LLPT is qualifying in nature; candidates must secure the Bank-prescribed minimum qualifying marks to be considered for final selection.
  • Candidates who fail to qualify the LLPT are treated as ineligible for final selection, irrespective of performance in other stages.
  • Candidates who indicate they studied the local language in Class 10/12 are exempt from LLPT, subject to submission of valid documentary evidence at verification.

Personal Interview

  • All candidates shortlisted after qualifying the Online Written Test will be called for interview.
  • The Personal Interview carries 50 marks.
  • Minimum qualifying marks: 45% (22.50 marks) for SC/ST candidates; 50% (25 marks) for other candidates.
  • Candidates who fail to secure minimum qualifying marks in the interview will be disqualified.

Final Selection

  • Final selection is based on combined performance in the Online Written Test and Personal Interview, subject to qualifying the LLPT (where applicable).

  • The merit list is prepared state-wise and category-wise.

How to Apply for PNB LBO Recruitment 2026

  1. Visit the official PNB website: https://pnb.bank.in/, under Recruitment/Career.
  2. Click "CLICK HERE FOR NEW REGISTRATION" and enter basic personal details to generate a Provisional Registration Number and Password (also sent via Email/SMS).
  3. Re-login using the Provisional Registration Number and Password to complete the application form.
  4. Upload scanned images of photograph, signature, left-hand thumb impression, and hand-written declaration as per prescribed specifications (see below).
  5. Use "SAVE AND NEXT" to verify details before clicking "COMPLETE REGISTRATION" - no changes are allowed after this step.
  6. Pay the applicable application fee through the online payment gateway (Debit Card, Credit Card, Net Banking, IMPS, Wallets, or UPI).
  7. On successful payment, an e-receipt will be generated.
  8. Take a printout of the submitted application form and e-receipt for personal record; do not send these to the Bank.

Applications are accepted online only, from 20.07.2026 to 09.08.2026, through https://pnb.bank.in/. No other mode of application will be accepted.

PNB LBO Recruitment 2026: Important Instructions

  • Candidates who have earlier worked in PNB or its merged/amalgamated entities and were discharged for reasons other than VRS/Resignation are not eligible to apply.
  • Candidates against whom there are adverse reports regarding character, antecedents, or moral turpitude are not eligible to apply.
  • There is no reservation for Ex-Servicemen in direct recruitment to Officer Cadre; however, age relaxation applies as per Government guidelines.
  • Selected candidates must execute an Indemnity Bond to serve the Bank for at least 3 years, or pay Rs. 2,00,000/- if they leave before completing 3 years of service.
  • Candidates must maintain a minimum CIBIL score of 680 or above at the time of joining. This is not a pre-condition to apply, and candidates with no bank account are not required to produce CIBIL status.
  • Selected candidates will be designated "Local Bank Officer" and will be on probation for 2 years from the date of joining.
  • After induction training, LBOs will be deployed within the Circles of the state for which they were selected, and will remain posted in that state until completion of 9 years of service or promotion to SMG Scale IV, whichever is earlier.
  • No Travelling Allowance is payable for the Online Test and LLPT. Unemployed SC/ST candidates called for interview will be paid actual to-and-fro 2nd Class Rail/Ordinary Bus fare.
  • Candidates must possess a valid Aadhaar card; the Bank may conduct Aadhaar verification at various stages.
  • Any dispute arising from this recruitment is subject to the sole jurisdiction of the Courts situated at NCT of Delhi.
  • The Bank reserves the right to cancel or modify the recruitment process at any stage without prior notice.

About IREL (India) Limited

IREL (India) Limited is a Mini Ratna Category-I Central Public Sector Undertaking under the administrative control of the Department of Atomic Energy, with its Corporate Office at Mumbai. The company operates Atomic Mineral Mining and Mineral Separation Plants at Chavara (Kerala), Manavalakurichi (Tamil Nadu), and Orissa Sands Complex — OSCOM (Odisha), producing Ilmenite, Rutile, Zircon, Sillimanite, and Garnet. It has also set up a Rare Earths Extraction Plant (REEP) in Odisha and a High Pure Rare Earths (HPRE) plant at RED, Aluva. IREL has joint ventures including IDCOL (Odisha), TAMIN (Tamil Nadu), and UKTMP JSC (Kazakhstan), along with a Rare Earth and Titanium Theme Park project in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh.

IREL Recruitment 2026 Eligibility Criteria

General Qualification Norms

  • All prescribed qualifications must be with First Class (60% marks in aggregate) for UR/OBC(NCL)/EWS candidates and 55% marks in aggregate for SC/ST candidates. This requirement does not apply to qualified CAs/CMAs/CSs.
  • Courses must be full-time/regular and recognized by the State/Central Government/UGC/AICTE, as applicable.
  • For non-technical posts, qualifications via Online/Distance Learning from recognized universities/institutions are also considered, subject to conditions.
  • If a course does not indicate percentage/first class, a conversion certificate from the university is required; in its absence, a minimum of 6 on a 10-point scale will be treated as 60%.

Experience Requirement for Government/PSU Candidates

Candidates from Central/State Govt./PSUs/Autonomous Organizations must possess a minimum of two years' experience in the immediate lower scale of pay (or equivalent) as on 10/08/2026, out of the total post-qualification experience required for the post.

How to Apply for IREL Recruitment 2026

  1. Visit the official IREL website: www.irel.co.in or the application portal directly.
  2. Click the apply link: https://cdn.digialm.com/EForms/configuredHtml/1258/100473/Index.html
  3. Step-I (Registration): Fill in Personal Details and Contact Details, then click "Generate OTP." Verify Mobile Number and Email ID using the OTPs received.
  4. Accept the terms and conditions, re-verify entered details, and click Submit. An Application Sequence Number (User ID) and Password will be sent via e-mail and SMS.
  5. Step-II (Filling the Application): Log in using the User ID and Password, then complete Personal Details, Additional Details, Communication Details, Qualification Details, and Declaration.
  6. Upload the required documents, including a recent passport-size photograph (white background, 100–200 KB, .jpg/.jpeg, 200 dpi, 3.5 cm x 4.5 cm) and signature (80–150 KB, .jpg/.jpeg).
  7. Preview the application to check for errors, then click Submit. Editing is not possible after submission.
  8. Pay the applicable application fee (Rs. 944/- or Rs. 354/- as applicable) through the online payment gateway.
  9. Print and retain the submitted Application Form and Payment Acknowledgement Slip for future reference.

Candidates should not wait until the last date to apply, as IREL will not be responsible for delays caused by last-minute rush.

IREL Recruitment 2026: Reservation & Relaxation Policy

  • Reservation and relaxation for OBC(NCL)/SC/ST/EWS/PwBD (40% and above disability)/Ex-servicemen candidates follow Government of India guidelines.
  • Reservation for PwBD is on a horizontal basis.
  • SC/ST/PwBD/ESM/Women/Internal candidates are exempted from the application fee but must pay the non-refundable processing fee of Rs. 354/-.
  • OBC(NCL) candidates must upload a valid certificate in the prescribed format and produce a certificate obtained on or after 01.04.2026 at the time of document verification.
  • EWS candidates must upload a valid Income & Asset Certificate and produce one valid for 2026-27 at document verification.
  • Category once selected in the online application form cannot be changed later.
  • Candidates belonging to OBC "Creamy Layer" are not entitled to OBC(NCL) concessions and must indicate their category as UR.

IREL Recruitment 2026: Important Instructions

  • Only Indian Nationals are eligible to apply.
  • Persons who have taken Voluntary Retirement (VRS) from Govt./PSUs, including IREL, are not eligible to apply.
  • Government/PSU employees should apply through proper channel or produce a No Objection Certificate (NOC) at the time of interview.
  • Intimation regarding test/interview will be sent only through e-mail.
  • Interviews may be conducted online (Video Conferencing) or face-to-face, depending on requirement.
  • Candidates called for face-to-face interview will be reimbursed to-and-fro III AC rail fare (E-1 to E-5 grades) or II AC rail fare (E-6 & E-7 grades) from the nearest railway station, by the shortest route.
  • Any legal dispute related to this recruitment falls under the exclusive jurisdiction of Courts/Forums/Tribunals at Mumbai.
  • Any corrigendum/addendum will be published only on the official website; no further press notifications will be issued.
  • Canvassing, directly or indirectly, will lead to disqualification.
  • PwBD candidates must meet the Physical Requirements and Functional Classifications specified for the post (see Annexure-I of the official notification).
